## The astrophysical neutrino flux {#icecube-diffuse-flux}

**IceCube, 2013**

A high-energy event excess established an astrophysical neutrino component.

::: {.question}
Which observable separates that component from the atmospheric background?
:::

::: {.notes}
Results occupy 30–44 minutes. Show a dated event sample with its atmospheric
prediction before the fitted astrophysical spectrum. Label confidence levels.

Source: [Spiering, section 4.1 and its primary references](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26436).
:::

## An independent measurement with Baikal-GVD {#baikal-diffuse-flux}

**Six seasons: April 2018 to March 2024**

The cascade analysis detects the diffuse astrophysical flux at $5.1\sigma$.

::: {.takeaway}
Different medium, instrumentation and reconstruction. An independent test.
:::

::: {.media-caption}
[Baikal-GVD, six-season analysis (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.01893)
:::

::: {.notes}
Compare spectra with the same flavour convention, units and energy interval.
The published power-law fit assumes equal flavour contributions. Do not
silently replace a per-flavour normalization with an all-flavour one.
:::

<!-- Visual slot: GVD energy distribution and correctly normalised comparison. -->

## The Milky Way in neutrinos {#galactic-neutrinos}

Cosmic rays interacting with Galactic matter produce diffuse emission.

Resolving individual accelerators is a further observational challenge.

::: {.notes}
Compare maps with explicit angular resolution and energy selection. Separate
the diffuse Galactic component from point-source claims. Include the latest
appropriate Baikal-GVD result when developing this block.

Source: [Spiering, section 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26436).
:::

<!-- Visual slot: aligned Galactic-coordinate maps in photons and neutrinos. -->

## TXS 0506+056 and multimessenger observations {#txs-0506}

- The 2017 neutrino alert and electromagnetic follow-up.
- The separate 2014–2015 excess in archival neutrino data.
- The Baikal-GVD event compatible with this direction in 2021.

::: {.notes}
Keep these datasets and their statistical questions distinct. Directional
compatibility does not prove the origin of an individual event. Use dated
significances, trial corrections and the latest reconstruction caveats.

Source: [D'Ammando, section 3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.30764).
:::

## KM3-230213A {#km3-230213a}

**An exceptionally energetic, nearly horizontal event**

The inferred neutrino energy is about $220\,\mathrm{PeV}$,
with a broad uncertainty interval.

Its source remains unknown.

::: {.media-caption}
[KM3NeT, Nature (2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-08543-1)
:::

::: {.notes}
The event occurred on 13 February 2023. The paper estimates the muon energy
at the detector separately from the parent neutrino energy. Include the
published uncertainty interval, spectral assumptions and exposure comparison
when developing the result. Do not imply an identified source or new physics.
:::

<!-- Visual slot: collaboration event display, with a physical length scale. -->

## Searches without a significant excess {#source-limits}

Upper limits test source models and population hypotheses.

Baikal-GVD's first track-based search examined 92 candidate objects.

No significant excess emerged from that analysis.

::: {.media-caption}
[Baikal-GVD, point-source constraints (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21261)
:::

::: {.notes}
Compare limits only for matched spectra and confidence conventions. One
example from a broader population search can illustrate why non-detections
are scientifically useful.
:::
